commands: jq '{package: (._embedded.facets[] | select(.key == "package") | {key,summary,operators,values}), literal: (._embedded.facets[] | select(.key == "library-literal") | {key,summary,operators,input_rules,requires,values}), target: (._embedded.facets[] | select(.key == "library-target") | {key,summary,operators}), cli: (._embedded.bindings[] | select(.consumer_kind == "Cli") | {gesture,input_rules,exposed_facets})}' /tmp/explain-usability-hal-domain/hal.json > /tmp/explain-usability-hal-domain/evidence-view.json; wc -c /tmp/explain-usability-hal-domain/evidence-view.json; cat /tmp/explain-usability-hal-domain/evidence-view.json

answer.matching: The positional package ID selects one exact package ID. The library-literal operand is matched as an ordinal substring of each decoded string-literal use in selected implementation libraries, so https:// need not be the entire literal.
answer.operand: Decoded UTF-16 text must be 1..1024 UTF-16 code units. Preserve whitespace, newlines, and case; do not normalize. Identical repeated operands collapse; distinct operands are incompatible. An empty values list does not mean no arbitrary operands are accepted: any decoded UTF-16 text satisfying these rules is accepted.
answer.framework: Supply the exact net8.0 framework through --tfm net8.0; library-literal and --tfm require each other. The package ID is exact, so it selects one candidate within the package-content limit of five.
answer.astral_600: No. Each astral Unicode character occupies two UTF-16 code units, so 600 occupy 1200, exceeding the 1024-unit maximum.

uncertainties: No package query was run, so the package's actual literal matches are unknown.
The embedded facet does not specify case-sensitivity of package ID equality; no claim about it is made.
